items.title: English Language in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Transforming Literary Expression in the Metamodern Era
items.abstract: The twenty-first century has witnessed an unprecedented convergence of language, technology, and artificial intelligence (AI), fundamentally reshaping literary production, interpretation, and dissemination. English, as the dominant language of digital communication and technological innovation, has become central to the global exchange of knowledge, creative expression, and computational systems. Simultaneously, AI technologies, particularly natural language processing and generative language models, have transformed traditional notions of authorship, creativity, and literary aesthetics. These developments have become especially significant within the framework of Metamodernism, a cultural paradigm characterized by oscillation between sincerity and irony, optimism and skepticism, reality and virtuality. The present study investigates the evolving role of the English language in the technological era and examines how AI influences the literature of the metamodern age. Employing a qualitative research methodology based on textual analysis and interdisciplinary literary criticism, the paper synthesizes insights from digital humanities, media studies, linguistic theory, and contemporary literary criticism. It argues that AI should not be viewed merely as a technological instrument but as a collaborative participant in literary production that challenges conventional definitions of creativity and textual authority. Furthermore, the study explores how English functions as the principal medium through which AI systems learn, generate, and disseminate literary texts, thereby reinforcing its global cultural influence. The findings suggest that while AI introduces ethical and aesthetic challenges, it also expands creative possibilities and redefines literary expression in the metamodern era.

items.title: Enhancing Patient Care and Nursing Practice Through AI-Driven Analysis of Patient Complaints: A Pilot Study
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in healthcare has shown promise for analyzing complex data and identifying patterns that can enhance clinical decision-making and patient care. Patient complaints represent a valuable yet underutilized data source for improving healthcare quality and patient safety. This study aimed to investigate whether an AI-driven model could effectively categorize patient complaints to extract actionable insights that support person-centered care and nursing practice to improve care quality. Method: An explorative study design was conducted as a pilot project. A total of 368 patient complaint reports collected by a Patients’ Advisory Committee were analyzed using AI-driven clustering and classification techniques. The complaints were pre-processed through text cleaning, tokenization, and vectorization before being analyzed with various clustering algorithms. Results: The AI-based classification identified four main areas that directly or indirectly influenced patients’ perceptions of care quality: (1) Care and Treatment, (2) Communication, (3) Administrative Management, and (4) Availability. These areas encompassed themes such as diagnostic delays, poor communication, fragmented administrative processes, and limited accessibility. The results highlighted that communication failures, insufficient empathy, and lack of continuity were central to patient dissatisfaction. Automated analysis enabled the identification of recurring issues and systemic weaknesses that traditional manual review methods often overlook. Conclusion: This pilot study demonstrates the feasibility and potential of using an AI-driven model to categorize patient complaints and identify patterns that may provide actionable insights for person-centered care and nursing practice to improve quality of care. The multilabel approach enabled an efficient and systematic analysis of complex complaints and may, following further validation, offer a scalable and consistent basis for understanding patient concerns. In nursing practice, integrating AI into patient feedback systems could support the earlier identification of recurring concerns and contribute to more responsive, evidence-informed, and person-centered quality improvement. However, larger datasets, independent expert validation, and careful consideration of ethical, legal, and governance requirements are needed before the model can be implemented more broadly.

items.title: Enhancing personalized learning pathways in vocational education through AI and big data analytics
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Big Data analytics are increasingly transforming vocational education by enabling personalized learning experiences and supporting data-driven educational practices. This study examines the influence of AI-powered personalized learning and Big Data analytics on student engagement, vocational skill development, learning efficiency, and overall program satisfaction at Vocational Colleges in Henan Province. A quantitative research design was adopted, and structured questionnaires were administered to 250 participants from the vocational education environment. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability and validity testing, ANOVA, and regression analysis to evaluate the proposed relationships among the study variables. The findings indicate positive participant perceptions of AI-based personalized learning, with high mean scores for AI personalization (4.215), student engagement (4.200), skill readiness (4.187), learning efficiency (4.210), and program satisfaction (4.220). Both regression and mediation analyses revealed positive associative and indirect links between AI personalization, the processing of big data, learner engagement and the vocational learning outcomes. However, ANOVA results did not show statistically significant effects of AI on skill readiness (p = 0.222), AI combined with Big Data on skill readiness (p = 0.258), AI on learning efficiency (p = 0.348), or AI on satisfaction (p = 0.348). Thus, the findings indicate positive participant perceptions and significant associative and mediating relationships, while the non-significant ANOVA results do not support direct effects of AI on several vocational learning outcomes.

items.title: Enterprise Agent Identity Governance Framework (EAIGF): A Policy-Mediated Identity and Access Governance Model for Autonomous Digital Workforce Systems
items.abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are evolving from passive decision-support tools into autonomous digital workers capable of planning, reasoning, invoking tools, accessing enterprise resources, and executing business actions with varying degrees of autonomy. While enterprises maintain mature governance models for human identities, service accounts, and application identities, existing Identity and Access Management (IAM) frameworks do not adequately address the governance challenges introduced by autonomous agents. Unlike conventional applications, agents dynamically determine execution paths, invoke reusable skills, delegate tasks to peer agents, and perform privileged actions across enterprise systems. These characteristics define a new class of enterprise identity that requires dedicated governance, authorization, and accountability controls. This paper proposes the Enterprise Agent Identity Governance Framework (EAIGF), which treats autonomous agents as first-class enterprise identities subject to lifecycle management, quantitative trust classification, privileged access governance, and end-to-end accountability. The framework's principal constructs form an identity layer comprising the Agent Identity Registry (AIR), the Agent Provisioning Certificate, Agent Trust Tiering driven by an explicit Agent Identity Risk Score (AIRS) formula, Agent Privileged Access Management (Agent-PAM), and a Delegated Trust Chain with Agent Identity Lineage for multi-agent accountability. These constructs are enforced through a policy-mediated runtime boundary that performs capability projection and risk-adaptive authorization. A reference implementation realizing the registry, the AIRS formula, capability projection, and risk-adaptive authorization correctly enforced all ten governance scenarios in the evaluation with zero false-permits on disallowed capabilities and a mean authorization overhead of approximately 0.015 ms per request. A larger randomized evaluation over 600 authorization requests across 80 agents and 25 reusable skills reproduced this result and, against a naive whole-skill authorization baseline, reduced the exposed capability surface by 66.7 percent while blocking every attempted privilege escalation through delegation. A synthetic financial-services walkthrough demonstrates how Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), Privileged Access Management (PAM), and Zero Trust principles extend to agentic environments. EAIGF provides a practical blueprint for governing autonomous agents at scale while preserving least privilege, accountability, and operational resilience.

items.title: Entre algoritmos y memoria: repensar la difusión del patrimonio cultural en la era de la IA
items.abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence in the field of cultural heritage has sparked debates that often oscillate between enthusiasm and apprehension. However, AI is no longer a future possibility but a present reality, already integrated into numerous processes of research, communication, and access to knowledge. From this perspective, the real challenge is not whether we should accept or reject AI, but rather how to incorporate it in a responsible, critical, and meaningful way that serves the objectives of heritage management. The most significant contribution of AI to cultural heritage does not lie primarily in the automation of tasks, but in its ability to expand and enrich the contexts through which heritage is understood, making specialized knowledge accessible to increasingly diverse audiences. Heritage research produces a vast amount of rigorous information that often remains confined to academic or professional environments. In this regard, artificial intelligence can help translate, connect, and disseminate such knowledge without compromising scientific rigor. From the perspective of heritage education, this capacity is particularly important, as the preservation of heritage largely depends on citizens’ ability to know, understand, and value it. Conservation is not achieved solely through legal protection measures or technical interventions; it also requires social awareness and public engagement. By facilitating access to knowledge and promoting new forms of interaction with cultural assets, AI can contribute to strengthening the relationship between communities and their heritage. Nevertheless, AI should always be understood as a tool rather than an end in itself. Critical judgment, interpretation, and scientific responsibility remain inherently human competencies that cannot be delegated to technology. Consequently, the greatest potential of artificial intelligence lies in helping heritage knowledge move beyond specialized circles and become a genuine public good, fostering a more informed, engaged, and culturally aware society.

items.title: Entrepreneurship-Based P5 Learning: Strengthening Teacher Professionalism through AI Assessment Development and Dissemination in Rural Schools
items.abstract: Elementary teachers in rural Indonesia face substantial barriers in delivering the entrepreneurship theme of the Projek Penguatan Profil Pelajar Pancasila (P5) [Project for Strengthening the Pancasila Learner Profile], the national program that grounds character education in Indonesia’s five founding principles, particularly in designing authentic assessment and in integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into project-based instruction. This study developed and validated an AI assessment model to strengthen teachers’ pedagogical, professional, social, and personal competencies. A five-stage Research and Development design comprised needs analysis, model design, expert validation, and staged field trials with a purposive sample of 19 teachers, followed by dissemination to all 91 teachers across the 12 schools of Gomo District, South Nias Regency. Only four teachers (21%) had received prior digital training. Expert validation confirmed feasibility across four domains (75.50–90.83%), and staged trials improved to an overall mean of 4.09. Pre-post comparisons showed gains in all four competency domains (+0.75 to +1.16), alongside a 63% rise in forum engagement and 96% platform uptime. Dissemination produced consistently positive reception across six constructs (overall M = 4.49, SD = 0.19), with perceived usefulness and behavioral intention rated most favorably. Embedding adaptive AI assessment within contextually grounded content can strengthen teacher professionalism in under-resourced rural schools.

items.title: Equitable and Consistent Support in New Zealand Law for Defence Force and Emergency Services Personnel (Report)
items.abstract: This paper examines why historical and current protections have not consistently provided early recognition, diagnosis, treatment, return to service, or whole-of-life care for military and emergency services personnel affected by service-related psychological and physical harm. It applies Dmitry Nikolaenko’s three regimes of scientific recognition—Accompanying Science, Warning Science, and Critical Reconstruction—to New Zealand Defence Force and emergency services contexts. The analysis considers psychological trauma, moral injury, cumulative occupational stress, cancers, and other chronic conditions associated with repeated exposure to toxins, toxic environments, and temperature-related stressors. Evidence is drawn from New Zealand legislation, operational arrangements, official reports, published research, compensation processes, and existing health data systems. The paper argues that Nikolaenko’s model remains applicable when attention shifts from environmental contamination to human health, but that Critical Reconstruction does not by itself specify what must happen after institutional non-recognition has been identified. Two further regimes are therefore proposed. Critical Practice addresses immediate protection, monitoring, data preservation, redress, and operational change. Critical Regeneration redesigns the relationship between scientific inquiry, governance responsibility, law, occupational health, and operational practice so that future harm is recognized and acted on earlier. Together, the five regimes form the Nikolaenko-Alexander Model.

items.title: Ergonomic Challenges and their Impact on Student Well-being: A Qualitative Study in a Nigerian University
items.abstract: Ergonomic challenges within university learning environments are increasingly recognized as important determinants of student health and academic performance.However, most studies in low-and middle-income countries focus on quantitative assessments, with limited attention to students' lived experiences.This study employed a qualitative descriptive design using open-ended responses collected via an online survey administered to 352 undergraduate students at the University of Calabar, Nigeria.Data were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis to explore students' experiences, perceived impacts, and coping mechanisms related to ergonomic challenges in their learning environments.Three major themes emerged: (1) Physical strain and bodily discomfort, characterized by musculoskeletal pain and visual strain due to non-adjustable furniture and poor environmental conditions; (2) Cognitive exhaustion and academic disruption, where discomfort impaired concentration, reduced engagement, and contributed to absenteeism; and (3) Institutional neglect and adaptive coping, highlighting the absence of supportive infrastructure and students' reliance on improvised strategies.These findings demonstrate that poor ergonomic conditions extend beyond physical discomfort to significantly affect mental well-being and academic outcomes.Ergonomic deficiencies in university settings represent a critical but underaddressed public health issue.Interventions should prioritize human-centered classroom design, inclusive infrastructure, and institutional policies that support student well-being.

items.title: ESTETIKA VISUAL DALAM DESAIN PARIWISATA KOTA DAN RESPON SOSIAL MASYARAKAT TERHADAP NILAI TAMBAH EKONOMI KREATIF BANDUNG: TINJAUAN AGAMA, BAHASA, DAN SASTRA SUNDA
items.abstract: This study aims to dissect the relationship between the Dynamics of the Urban Space Design Process (X1) and the Effectiveness of Sustainable Tourism Infrastructure Development (X2) through the lens of linguistics, literature, and Sundanese religious cosmology in Bandung. An explanatory sequential Mixed Methods approach was used by distributing questionnaires to 400 respondents in Braga, Cihapit, Dago, and Cilaki, followed by in-depth interviews based on literary discourse analysis. Statistical data processing using SPSS showed that the correlation between X1 and welfare recovery (Y) had a positive influence with a determination coefficient of $R^2 = 0.082$ and significance $p = 0.087$. Qualitatively, spatial planning that ignores local language toponymy and the philosophy of Tri Tangtu di Buana triggers social resistance. Modern urban design often erases the traces of oral literature and the religious memory of communal societies. This study found that successful tourism infrastructure is not only determined by the ergonomics of asphalt and concrete but by the spatial layout's ability to maintain the dialectic of silih asih, silih asah, silih asuh. The integration of the Sundanese Linguistic Landscape and inclusive design is the main key to the resilience of tourism MSMEs. Therefore, urban revitalization must restore the spiritual soul of the area to avoid cultural uprooting.

items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence offers new opportunities to strengthen self-directed learning in nursing education when its integration is supported by a structured pedagogical design. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of the E-PAGIA strategy, organized into planning, construction, self-monitoring, and interaction/transfer stages, on self-directed learning among nursing students. A quantitative, quasi-experimental, longitudinal study was conducted with 128 students, distributed between an experimental group and a control group, with 64 participants in each. The intervention lasted eight weeks. Self-directed learning was assessed using the Self-Directed Learning Instrument, considering both the overall score and its dimensions. The groups showed comparable baseline scores. Following the intervention, the experimental group increased its mean overall score from 65.00 to 82.35 points, whereas the control group increased from 65.75 to 69.46. Improvements in the experimental group were observed across all four dimensions and were particularly pronounced in learning motivation and planning and implementation. Analysis adjusted for baseline scores confirmed significant differences between groups and showed a large effect associated with the strategy. The findings indicate that E-PAGIA can foster self-directed learning when generative artificial intelligence is integrated as cognitive support within a pedagogical sequence that preserves students' intellectual responsibility, teacher mediation, and critical verification of information. The study concludes that E-PAGIA represents a relevant pedagogical innovation for nursing education.

items.title: Ethical Boundaries in Human-AI Collaborative Decision Systems: A Review
items.abstract: This review covers human–artificial intelligence collaboration in making decisions, observing how scholarship has moved from thinking of AI as a passive tool to considering it as an active actor in healthcare, management, and ethics. While AI systems provide for efficient data processing and pattern recognition, humans provide contextual understanding, ethical judgment, creativity, and accountability. Previous literature suggests that well-designed collaboration between humans and AI may outperform completely automated decision-making. However, several key challenges persist, like bias, lack of transparency, miscalibrated trust, poorly defined distribution of roles, and accountability gaps. To handle these concerns, human-centered design, explainability in AI, well-articulated guidelines on ethical consideration, and mechanisms that effectively introduce oversight remain at the core of literature. These approaches jointly try to ensure that human–AI decision-making systems are fair, accountable, and trustworthy in high-stakes and critical settings

items.title: EVALUASI PROGRAM AI CHATBOT ANSIA DI PERGURUAN TINGGI: ANALISIS MODEL CIPP (CONTEXT, INPUT, PROCESS, PRODUCT)
items.abstract: This study aims to evaluate ANSIA (SIDIA Assistant), an artificial intelligence -based chatbot program at Universitas Negeri Surabaya, using the CIPP (Context, Input, Process, Product) evaluation model. A descriptive-evaluative qualitative approach was employed. Data were collected through in-depth interviews and document analysis involving developers from the Directorate of Digital Learning Innovation (DIPD) at UNESA as key informants, as well as six lecturers and 19 students from the Office Administration Education undergraduate study program, cohorts 2024 and 2025, as primary informants. Data credibility was examined through source triangulation, and the data were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman interactive model. The evaluation revealed four major gaps. In the context component, ANSIA was developed without a formal needs assessment, resulting in a gap in user awareness. In the input component, server infrastructure and WhatsApp integration were not adequately supported by a dedicated budget, formal socialization, or sufficient operational guidelines. In the process component, an increase in aggregate server-log access did not fully reflect student use of ANSIA at the study-program level. Interview findings indicated that preferences for commercial artificial intelligence tools and limitations in the internal knowledge base were factors associated with low utilization. In the product component, a discrepancy emerged between developers’ claims of 24-hour service availability and users’ experiences in accessing and using the system. The study recommends expanding the scientific knowledge base, providing visual user guides, allocating a dedicated budget, and integrating ANSIA into teaching and learning activities. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi program chatbot berbasis artificial intelligence, yaitu ANSIA (Asisten SIDIA), di Universitas Negeri Surabaya menggunakan model evaluasi CIPP (Context, Input, Process, Product). Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain deskriptif evaluatif. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam dan dokumentasi yang melibatkan pengembang dari Direktorat Inovasi Pembelajaran Digital (DIPD) UNESA sebagai informan kunci serta enam dosen dan 19 mahasiswa Program Studi S1 Pendidikan Administrasi Perkantoran angkatan 2024 dan 2025 sebagai informan utama. Keabsahan data diperiksa melalui triangulasi sumber, sedangkan analisis data menggunakan model interaktif Miles dan Huberman. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan empat kesenjangan utama. Pada komponen context, pengembangan ANSIA tidak didahului asesmen kebutuhan formal sehingga ditemukan kesenjangan kesadaran (awareness gap) pengguna. Pada komponen input, dukungan infrastruktur server dan integrasi WhatsApp belum diimbangi anggaran khusus, sosialisasi formal, serta panduan operasional yang memadai. Pada komponen process, peningkatan jumlah akses berdasarkan log server agregat tidak sepenuhnya mencerminkan pemanfaatan ANSIA oleh mahasiswa di tingkat program studi. Temuan wawancara menunjukkan bahwa kecenderungan menggunakan artificial intelligence komersial dan keterbatasan basis pengetahuan internal menjadi faktor yang berkaitan dengan rendahnya pemanfaatan tersebut. Pada komponen product, terdapat perbedaan antara klaim pengembang mengenai ketersediaan layanan selama 24 jam dan pengalaman pengguna dalam mengakses serta memanfaatkan sistem. Penelitian ini merekomendasikan perluasan basis pengetahuan ilmiah, penyediaan panduan visual, pengalokasian anggaran khusus, dan integrasi ANSIA dalam kegiatan pembelajaran.

items.title: Evaluating Instrument-Centered AI Agents for Table-Top Science Experiments
items.abstract: Reliable evaluation of AI agents for table-top science experiments has remained elusive because live instruments are hard to reset and share at scale, while instrument statefulness and safety constraints complicate evaluation. We introduce instrMCP and q-devBench, an evaluation stack for instrument-centered AI agents in table-top experiments. instrMCP connects coding agents to scientific instruments through the Model Context Protocol, serving as the instrument-access harness. q-devBench reconstructs 37 real experimental tasks from condensed-matter physics as virtual QCoDeS instruments covering quantum electronic transport, scanning probe imaging, and calibration workflows. q-devBench exposes reproducible failure modes in laboratory-agent systems while preserving realistic instrument-control workflows. Across a range of commercial coding-agent configurations, current systems already show substantial operational competence, satisfying 70-83% of measurement-related rubric criteria. The main bottleneck is scientific analysis, where performance falls to 28-46%. In an analysis-only ablation in which agents receive clean reference datasets without running the virtual measurement session, analysis performance improves substantially, closing roughly two thirds of the difference between the measurement and analysis scores. This suggests that much of the deficit arises from the measurement-session context, including tool-use overhead, longer context, measurement-planning decisions, and possible acquisition errors, while a residual scientific-reasoning gap remains. Together, instrMCP and q-devBench provide a practical sandbox for benchmarking, diagnosing, and improving laboratory AI harnesses, and establish a route from controlled virtual evaluation to future live-hardware validation.

items.title: Evolution of Financial AI: From Statistical Models to Agentic AI
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in finance has evolved from statistical learning and machine learning for structured prediction, through deep learning and foundation models for representation learning, language understanding, and reasoning, to retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-grounded reasoning and agentic AI for autonomous planning and execution. In this paper, we examine how researchers and practitioners can select and apply AI methods in finance. We first show that the major paradigms of financial AI address fundamentally different classes of problems, rather than forming a strict hierarchy of capability. We then review the current state of research on AI in finance and trace how these paradigms have reshaped financial data, financial tasks, decision support, and human-AI collaboration. Building on this, we propose practical guidelines for matching AI paradigms to task characteristics, and show that more advanced models, such as foundation models or autonomous agents, are not universally superior. We conclude by outlining open challenges for researchers and practitioners working toward reliable financial AI.

items.title: Evolutionary processes in corporate governance: pedagogical research perspectives.
items.abstract: Corporate governance is one of the areas most affected by the economic, technological and social transformations that have taken place in recent years. The emergence of complex digital ecosystems, the automation of decision-making processes and the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) are redefining not only the way organisations operate (Abriani, 2020), but also the epistemological and value-based assumptions on which strategic decisions are founded. Modern business is undergoing a profound transformation (Rossi, 2012). Corporate governance, traditionally understood as a set of rules, structures and mechanisms designed to ensure the control and management of the enterprise, now tends to take on a dynamic and relational form, in which human actors, technologies, information networks and socio-cultural contexts interact (Fenwick et al., 2018). At the same time, the issue of inclusion and organisational well-being has taken on increasing importance: organisations are increasingly called upon to respond not only to economic performance targets, but also to demands for equity, social sustainability and the valuing of differences (Schneider, 2022). items.title: Executive Function Decay: Why Managerial Judgment Fails Under Pressure and How Organizations Can Respond
items.abstract: Mental-health strain has become a routine feature of organizational life, yet managers and organizations continue to struggle to explain why capable employees make avoidable errors, why teams lose coordination under pressure, and why judgment quality deteriorates during periods of sustained stress. This article argues that executive function decay—the temporary or chronic degradation of working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility—is a central but underrecognized mechanism linking mental strain to workplace performance failures.Drawing on research from cognitive neuroscience, clinical psychology, and organizational behavior, I explain how common forms of mental-health morbidity and burnout impair the cognitive capacities that support judgment, emotional regulation, and adaptive decision-making. I show how executive function decay produces predictable patterns of managerial behavior, team dysfunction, and organizational drift that are misattributed to motivation, attitude, or character.The article introduces a multilevel framework connecting executive function impairment to outcomes at the individual, team, and organizational levels. I then translate this framework into practical implications for leaders and HR systems, highlighting how job design, leadership behavior, workload architecture, and organizational norms can either stabilize or erode cognitive capacity. By reframing mental health as a decision-quality and organizational design issue, this article offers managers and scholars a practical lens for improving judgment, coordination, and resilience under pressure.

items.title: Expert system for motorcycle damage diagnosis using certainty factor and case-based reasoning methods
items.abstract: Motorcycles are the main mode of transportation that requires maintenance due to damage. Unfortunately, damage detection on motorcycles remains traditional, despite the potential for expert systems and artificial intelligence (AI) to facilitate more straightforward diagnosis for both motorcycle users and mechanics. That is why this research aims to develop a system with an expert system approach to diagnose damage to a motorcycle. This research applies the certainty factor (CF) expert system approach and the case-based reasoning (CBR) AI method. The study found that the expert system using the CBR method outperforms the CF method in diagnosing motorcycle damage. The CF expert system method achieves an accuracy performance of 98%. In comparison, the CBR expert system method achieves an accuracy of up to 100%, or can be equated with human mechanics in diagnosing motorcycle damage. The finding implies that CBR can effectively replace human experts in detecting motorcycle damage.

items.title: EXPLAINABLE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR FORMATIVE SUPPORT ALLOCATION IN HIGHER EDUCATION: A HUMAN-SUPERVISED DECISION ARCHITECTURE AND SYNTHETIC SIMULATION
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence and learning analytics can identify patterns of learning risk earlier and support more differentiated allocation of formative support in higher education. Yet predictive accuracy does not by itself make an educational decision valid: evidence must be interpretable in relation to learning goals, explanations must not be confused with causal diagnosis, and final support decisions should remain subject to professional review and learner participation. This article develops a human-supervised decision architecture and computationally illustrates its predictive and support-allocation components through a reproducible simulation of 10,000 synthetic learner-course observations without using personal data. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were compared under class imbalance. Decision thresholds were selected on a validation subset by minimizing a weighted decision-cost function in which missing an at-risk learner was assigned greater weight than generating an additional support-review action. On the independent test set, XGBoost achieved ROC-AUC = 0.910, PR-AUC = 0.764, recall = 0.902, F1 = 0.612, and Matthews correlation coefficient = 0.526 at a threshold of 0.220. Mean absolute SHAP values indicated that formative assessment score, task completion, attendance, prior achievement, self-regulation, engagement, learning progress, and study consistency contributed most strongly to predictions. Under the stated scenario assumptions, the AI-assisted allocation strategy produced an illustrative weighted decision cost that was 62.4% lower than a reactive end-of-term strategy and 26.9% fewer review/support actions than a simple rule-based strategy. The scenario models alert allocation and review workload only; it does not model teacher acceptance, intervention implementation, learner response, or learning effects. The methodological contribution is the integration of cost-sensitive thresholding, a mandatory teacher decision gate, SHAP-informed pedagogical reason codes, learner challenge and data correction, and workload-aware threshold governance within one auditable formative-assessment architecture. The reported metrics therefore illustrate the predictive and allocation logic of the architecture rather than the effectiveness of the pedagogical system as a whole.

items.abstract: Modern law enforcement agencies face the dual challenge of managing complex public safety threats while maintaining strict institutional accountability. This paper explores the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), automation, and advanced digital tools within modern policing frameworks. By analyzing current implementations—including predictive policing algorithms, automated facial recognition, automated license plate readers (ALPRs), and AI-driven evidence management systems—this study assesses how these technologies enhance operational efficiency, accelerate response times, and optimize resource allocation. Furthermore, the paper addresses critical systemic challenges, specifically targeting algorithmic bias, citizen privacy concerns, data security vulnerabilities, and the regulatory frameworks required to govern automated decision-making. Ultimately, this research provides a balanced framework for law enforcement executives and policymakers, demonstrating how agencies can leverage cutting-edge technical innovation while upholding the core principles of ethical, transparent, and community-oriented justice

items.title: Explanation and Validation as Conditions for Trust in Judicial AI in Bangladesh
items.abstract: Abstract Judicial artificial intelligence requires grounds for warranted reliance rather than confidence alone. This study examines how respondents in Bangladesh distinguish understandable reasons, independent validation and opportunities to challenge AI-supported recommendations. A cross-sectional analysis of 385 adult, AI-aware respondents uses seven questionnaire items without treating their mixed normative and conditional wording as a validated explainability-trust scale. The analysis combines paired endorsement comparisons, proportional-odds models with robust covariance, multiplicity adjustment and paired-outcome coefficient comparisons. Independent-validation-contingent trust was endorsed by 247 respondents (64.2%), compared with 215 (55.8%) for explanation-contingent trust: a paired difference of 8.3 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 1.6–15.1; Holm-adjusted p = .021). Access to review or appeal received greater endorsement than the ability to question recommendations (85.2% versus 65.2%; difference 20.0 points, 95% interval 14.3–25.7). None of the eight focal associations between four governance expectations and the two trust propositions remained distinguishable from zero after Holm adjustment. The joint test of differences between the four outcome-specific coefficients was also inconclusive (p = .236). These findings identify a descriptive separation between explanations, validation and remedies while providing limited adjusted evidence about how those expectations align within respondents. The predominantly student sample does not establish judicial practice, actual reliance or causal effects of explanations. The article develops a layered account of judicial AI governance that connects understandable reasons with independent evaluation and effective review, and specifies a measurement and experimental agenda for testing calibrated reliance.

items.title: Exploring Artificial Intelligence-Generated Transcripts for Supporting Students Who Are Hard of Hearing: A Preliminary Analysis of Transcription Errors in Subject Lectures
items.abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) may help students who are hard of hearing review spoken explanations, but transcription errors could affect access to course content. This preliminary study examined ASR errors in three Korean EBS lectures (language, mathematics, and chemistry) and an English Technology, Entertainment, Design (TED) talk. Each lecture was played on an iPad in a quiet room and transcribed using Clova Note (Naver Corporation, Seongnam, Korea) and Plaud (Plaud Inc., San Francisco, CA, USA). The outputs were compared with reference transcripts using word error rate (WER) and character error rate (CER). For Korean, WER was calculated using space-delimited eojeols; for English, it was calculated using words. In the Korean language lecture, WERs were 20.27% for Clova Note (Naver Corporation) and 13.85% for Plaud (Plaud Inc.); in mathematics, 42.78% and 54.33%; and in chemistry, 28.62% and 28.44%, respectively. In the TED talk, WERs were 3.88% and 3.10%. In mathematics, the ranking of the two tools differed between WER and CER. Error rates varied across materials and measures, but these data cannot establish comparative performance across languages or benefits for students. Future studies should examine errors in key course content and evaluate how students use verified transcripts to understand lectures.

items.title: Exploring the Power of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Improving the Teaching of Business Education Courses in Government Tertiary Institutions in Rivers State
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly improving the teaching and learning process globally. Therefore, this study determined exploring the power of artificial intelligence (AI) for improving the teaching of business education courses in government tertiary institutions in Rivers State. Two research questions guided the study and two null hypotheses were tested. Descriptive survey research design was adopted. From a population of 99 lecturers, a census survey sampling was employed. A four-point response options questionnaire was used for data collection, and it was validated by three experts. The reliability of the instrument was established using Cronbach’s alpha which yielded coefficients of 0.79 and 0.78. Mean and Standard Deviation were used to answer the two research questions and measure the spread in respondents` opinions, while oneway analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to test the two null hypotheses at 0.05 level of significance. Findings revealed that all the types of AI listed were highly needed to be explored, and were very highly powerful for improving the teaching of business education courses. From the findings, it was concluded that if AI is included in the teaching of business education courses, it will transform the programme positively, lead to AI skills development and enable the learners to acquire the needed AI employability skills for the global workplace. Therefore, among other things, it was recommended that AI should be included in the business education curriculum through yearly internal curriculum review by lecturers in collaboration with their institutions and a five-year national review by all levels of government.

items.title: Eyes on Attention: AI-Based Webcam Assessment of Sustained Attention
items.abstract: This study examined the feasibility of an artificial intelligence system using webcam eye tracking to estimate sustained attention performance. In a controlled laboratory study, 129 participants (mean age: 25.98 ± 2.07 years; 83.7% female) completed the AX Continuous Performance Task. Performance was operationalized as a reciprocal-log index of correct-response reaction time, with higher values indicating faster responses. Six visual scanning features were captured, and five composite models were compared: one literature-based and four derived from experimental data. All showed significant in-sample associations with performance. The weighted composite incorporating all six features provided the best in-sample fit, but participant-level split-half cross-validation yielded a modest out-of-sample association (r = 0.19). Univariate analyses linked better performance to faster jumps and lower length and speed irregularity. These findings provide preliminary evidence for webcam-derived gaze features in cognitive assessment under laboratory conditions, with further validation needed before integration into human–computer interaction applications.

items.title: Factors affecting with the implementation of the occupational health and safety management system at Tuan Besar Syarif Idrus Regional General Hospital, Kubu Raya regency, West Kalimantan province
items.abstract: Occupational Safety and Health Management System (SMK3) is essential to protect hospital workers and support safe and quality healthcare services. However, its implementation may vary according to organizational and operational conditions, while evidence regarding the factors associated with SMK3 implementation at the regional hospital level remains limited. This study aimed to analyze the factors associated with SMK3 implementation at Tuan Besar Syarif Idrus Regional General Hospital, Kubu Raya Regency, West Kalimantan. An analytical quantitative study with a cross-sectional design was conducted among 180 employees. From a total workforce of 210 employees, 30 non-healthcare employees were allocated for instrument validity and reliability testing. A total of 140 respondents were selected using proportionate stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Spearman rank correlation and multiple linear regression with a significance level of 0.05. The results showed significant positive associations between SMK3 implementation and OHS policy (r = 0.408), management commitment (r = 0.505), human resource competence (r = 0.377), facilities and infrastructure (r = 0.659), and work environment (r = 0.306), with all p < 0.001. The multivariable regression model was significant (F = 34.721; p < 0.001) and explained 56.4% of the variance in SMK3 implementation (R² = 0.564). Facilities and infrastructure were the only significant independent predictor (β = 0.562; p < 0.001). These findings indicate that strengthening the availability, adequacy, accessibility, and maintenance of safety facilities and infrastructure should be prioritized to improve SMK3 implementation, supported by effective policies, management commitment, competent human resources, and a safe work environment.

items.title: Fairness, Bias, and Explainability in Detection AI
items.abstract: As AI system for detection has migrated from purely experimental demonstrations to an integral part of police, welfare, healthcare, and immigration systems, so has the lack of visibility for individuals being classified by those systems regarding how the systems work (and therefore how they can contest or correct the results produced by the systems). This chapter considers the problems of fairness and bias and explainability within detection AI using multiple in-depth case studies from the United States, the Netherlands, and India as examples of these issues as viewed through alternative ethical values derived from Sub-Saharan Africa, Indigenous and Confucian ethics. This chapter provides an argument supported by empirical research, general court documents, and regulations published between 2017 and 2025 that fair detection AI is a characteristic of a complete sociotechnical system rather than just the algorithmic part of the system. This chapter develops the concepts of the proxy problem and the opacity problem and shows how both recur across jurisdictions and decision domains. This chapter proposes a principle of contextual transparency, under which the explanation a detection system produces must serve the actual epistemic needs of the people affected by the system, in the contexts where the system’s outputs matter.

items.title: Faktor-faktor yang Berhubungan dengan Produktivitas Kerja Perawat di Rumah Sakit: Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Nurses’ work productivity is a strategic indicator of hospital service quality, as nurses are directly involved in patient care, documentation, interprofessional communication, and continuous patient safety efforts. This study aimed to examine the factors associated with nurses’ work productivity in hospitals. This study employed a systematic literature review method guided by the PRISMA 2020 statement and the PECO framework. The literature search was conducted through Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and PubMed for primary studies published in Indonesian or English between 2021 and 2026. A total of 20 articles were included in the qualitative synthesis. The reviewed studies indicated that workload, occupational stress, fatigue, motivation, discipline, income, work environment, shift system, management support, and individual characteristics were associated with nurses’ productivity. Workload emerged as the most consistently reported factor, while age and educational background tended to influence productivity through physical capacity, experience, professional competence, and maturity in decision-making. Improving nurses’ productivity requires integrated hospital occupational health and safety management through workload control, improvement of the physical work environment, fatigue prevention, fair task distribution, and competency development. Keywords: Nurse Productivity, Workload, Physical Work Environment, Age, Education. ABSTRAK Produktivitas kerja perawat merupakan indikator strategis mutu pelayanan rumah sakit karena perawat berperan langsung dalam asuhan pasien, dokumentasi, komunikasi antarprofesi, dan keselamatan pasien secara berkelanjutan. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk mengkaji faktor yang berhubungan dengan produktivitas kerja perawat di rumah sakit. Metode penelitian menggunakan systematic literature review dengan acuan PRISMA 2020 dan kerangka PECO. Penelusuran literatur dilakukan melalui Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, dan PubMed terhadap studi primer berbahasa Indonesia atau Inggris yang terbit pada tahun 2021-2026. Sebanyak 20 artikel diinklusi dalam sintesis kualitatif. Studi yang direview menunjukkan bahwa beban kerja, stres kerja, kelelahan, motivasi, disiplin, penghasilan, lingkungan kerja, sistem shift, dukungan manajemen, dan karakteristik individu berhubungan dengan produktivitas perawat. items.title: Fear and Fun: Dual Impact of AI Anxiety and Perceived Enjoyment on Acceptance Intention of Generative AI Tools
items.abstract: With the pervasive integration of generative artificial intelligence across diverse social domains, user acceptance intention manifests a distinctive coexistence of "fun and fear." Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model, this investigation develops an expanded model by integrating perceived enjoyment, AI anxiety, and privacy concerns, whilst assessing the moderating influence of professional background. Based on 486 valid questionnaires and structural equation modeling, the model shows acceptable fit (/df = 1.88, RMSEA = 0.043, CFI/TLI > 0.90). Perceived enjoyment strengthens attitude (β = 0.324, p < 0.001) and perceived usefulness (β = 0.284, p < 0.001), while AI anxiety reduces perceived usefulness (β = -0.296, p < 0.001) and privacy concern weakens attitude (β = -0.148, p = 0.021); the core TAM path is supported (ATT BI: β = 0.643, p < 0.001; BI USE: β = 0.535, p < 0.001). By contrast, H7, H8, and H10 are not supported (p > 0.05), and professional background shows negligible moderation. These results suggest that promoting generative AI requires enhancing enjoyable interaction while reducing anxiety and privacy risks.

items.title: Feeding AI with heritage is not enough: the limits of data must remain interpretable
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is used to describe, organise and interpret cultural heritage collections, yet discussion often focuses on what systems can produce rather than on the knowledge embodied in their data. This contribution approaches that problem through underwater archaeology, where the material traces of a shipwreck are encountered through historical documents, nautical charts, acoustic surveys, photographs, oral testimony and family memories. The identification of the Brazilian auxiliary ship Vital de Oliveira, torpedoed in 1944, offers a case for examining how evidence converge without becoming interchangeable. Historical records, bathymetric products and personal accounts arise from distinct processes and support different kinds of claims. Their integration therefore cannot be reduced to technical interoperability or persuasive reconstruction. Drawing on debates in digital archaeology, archival studies and the ethics of artificial intelligence, we argue that responsible heritage applications require attention to four interrelated conditions: provenance, uncertainty, interpretive plurality and responsibility. Provenance and paradata make the circumstances of data production traceable; uncertainty distinguishes observation from inference; plurality keeps divergent interpretations open to scrutiny; and responsibility addresses consent, rights, institutional decisions and the sensitivities surrounding human memory. These principles are proposed as a curatorial orientation, not as an implemented computational ontology or an assessment of an operational AI system. Although grounded in underwater cultural heritage, the argument extends to museums, libraries, archives and digital collections. The central challenge is not simply to make heritage legible to artificial intelligence, but to ensure that the limits, omissions and mediations of its evidentiary foundations remain legible to people as well.

items.title: Feeling Like a Number: How AI’s Neglect of Uniqueness Undermines User Acceptance in Online Medical Consultations
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) promises greater efficiency and accessibility in online medical consultation (OMC). However, user acceptance, particularly among older adults, remains low. This paradox is not fully explained by cognitive-centric models like the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). This study investigates uniqueness neglect as a critical psychological barrier induced by standardized algorithmic interactions. Two between-subjects experiments manipulated consultation type (AI vs. human doctor) to induce differential perception of uniqueness neglect. Results revealed that AI-doctor consultation triggered stronger uniqueness neglect, which reduced acceptance through serial mediators of perceived usefulness and emotional response. The study also provides evidence that activating higher perceived usefulness is an effective intervention. Theoretically, our findings reveal a cognitive-affective serial mechanism extending beyond utilitarian model(s) of resistance to AI services. Practically, OMC platforms should design AI interactions that proactively affirm functional value to compensate for standardized procedure.

items.title: From Academic Integrity to Professional Formation in Generative AI–Supported Nursing Education: Integrative Review
items.abstract: Abstract Background The rapid integration of generative AI (GenAI) into nursing education has prompted widespread concern about academic integrity and assessment validity. However, this dominant discourse may obscure a more fundamental challenge: preparing nursing students for clinical practice environments where AI already mediates triage, diagnostics, documentation, and clinical decision-making. Objective This integrative review examines how GenAI is conceptualized within the nursing education literature and investigates the extent to which current discourse addresses professional formation rather than academic compliance. Methods Following Whittemore and Knafl’s integrative review methodology, a systematic search of PubMed, Google Scholar, and SciSpace (Typeset) was conducted for literature published between January 2022 and February 2026. Two reviewers independently screened 456 records, with 119 papers meeting the inclusion criteria. The methodological quality of empirical studies was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Corpus-level descriptive mapping quantified dominant themes and conceptual patterns, while an interpretive synthesis examined how GenAI was framed and the extent to which professional formation elements, including identity, moral agency, and clinical judgment, were addressed. Results Of the 119 unique studies analyzed, 84% (n=100) predominantly framed GenAI as a content-generation tool and academic integrity threat. Only 35.3% (n=42) conceptualized AI as a pedagogical tool, and a critical gap was identified in professional formation: identity formation was addressed in only 10% (n=12) of papers and moral agency in just 5% (n=6). Explicit acknowledgment that AI already routinely mediates frontline clinical decisions (eg, sepsis alerts and fall risk algorithms) in current practice settings was notably absent. The discourse emphasizes governance and faculty literacy, but sustained curricula addressing nurse identity in AI-mediated care remain underdeveloped. Conclusions Current nursing education discourse predominantly frames AI as a writing tool and an academic integrity concern, failing to prepare students for the algorithmic practice environments they will inhabit. Nursing education must reframe AI as a professional formation issue, explicitly addressing how algorithms reshape clinical judgment, moral agency, and professional identity.

items.title: From Automation to Augmentation
items.abstract: The rapid emergence of generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) is reshaping human resource (HR) management, requiring HR managers to integrate traditional HR expertise with AI-specific competencies. Despite growing research on AI-enabled human resource management, few studies have identified the competencies required by hybrid HR–Gen AI managers, particularly in emerging-market contexts. This study aims to identify and analyze these competencies in the Tunisian context and to develop an empirically grounded competency framework for AI-enabled HR transformation. Under an interpretivist paradigm and an inductive, qualitative approach, 12 semistructured interviews were conducted with hybrid HR–Gen AI managers. Using the MAXQDA tool, thematic analysis identified 49 competency codes grouped into seven competency categories: strategic, change management, human and interpersonal, technological and technical, analytic, ethical, and basic competencies. Seven individual competencies were mentioned by more than 50% of respondents, while “Gen AI-driven HR task automation” and “data privacy and confidentiality management” were identified as the most frequently cited, with each identified by 10 of the 12 participants. The findings also point to the relevance of ethical awareness, critical thinking, and a human-centered mindset in managing Gen AI-enabled HR transformation. The proposed competency framework can inform HR workforce development and organizational strategies for the responsible and effective integration of Gen AI into HR practices.

items.title: From Behavioral Instructions to Perceptual Goals: Manipulating Anthropomorphism in Human-AI Communication Experiments
items.abstract: Researchers commonly manipulate chatbot anthropomorphism through social cues, whose effects vary and may introduce unintended perceptual differences. Generative AI enables an alternative: manipulating perceived characteristics through natural-language prompting. Two online experiments (N = 84 each) evaluated behavior-prescriptive and perception-goal prompting for manipulating anthropomorphism. Study 1 found no significant differences in anthropomorphism. Study 2 found significant differences in general, mindful, and mindless anthropomorphism (ds = .86–.95), without significant differences in response coherence or perceived intelligence. These findings provide initial empirical support for perception-goal prompting and suggest broader methodological possibilities for manipulating perceived chatbot characteristics in human–AI communication research.

items.title: From Child-Centred Needs to Engineering Design Requirements: A Framework for Adaptive Interviewing Systems in Sensitive Judicial Procedures
items.abstract: Child interviewing in sensitive judicial procedures requires environments and systems that accommodate communication (COM), ergonomic (ERG), sensory/environmental (SEN), safety/privacy (SPR), and functional needs. However, child-sensitive recommendations are not always formulated as engineering specifications directly applicable to product and system development. This study proposes the Adaptive Child Interviewing System Framework (ACISF), a structured approach for translating multidisciplinary evidence into engineering requirements for adaptive child-centred interviewing systems. Child needs (CNs) are systematically translated into functional requirements (FRs), design requirements (DRs), and engineering parameters (EPs), with the resulting relationships consolidated within a Child Need–Engineering Requirement Matrix (CNERM). Adaptability is structured through common (C), age-adaptive (AA), and individually configurable (IC) requirements. The 6–10- and 10–14-year groups provide initial configuration bands, while individual configurability accommodates variation beyond age alone. The framework integrates requirements across five design domains and is demonstrated through the conceptual development of an adaptive child-interviewing cabin addressing spatial, anthropometric, accessibility, environmental, privacy, and safety considerations. The ACISF provides a traceable requirements-engineering architecture connecting child-centred evidence with implementable design solutions and supporting subsequent technical specification, prototype development, expert assessment, usability evaluation, and empirical validation.

items.title: From Compliance to Responsible AI: A Bibliometric Study on Educational Data Governance and Student Privacy (2015-2025)
items.abstract: This study maps the development of research on educational data governance and student privacy between 2015 and 2025. It follows the structure of a bibliometric trend review and uses a Scopus-derived record set of 313 articles to analyze the analytical workflow, including annual output, keyword co-occurrence, thematic evolution, policy turning points, and research collaboration. The study is guided by three questions: how the volume of research changed, how the dominant vocabulary moved from learning analytics and ownership to compliance and responsible artificial intelligence, and which problems remained unresolved across the period. The results show five connected phases. From 2015 to 2017, research was organized around learning analytics, educational data mining, student tracking, data ownership, and informed consent. After the General Data Protection Regulation became applicable on May 25, 2018, the literature moved toward data protection, compliance, governance frameworks, and institutional responsibility. The COVID-19 period increased attention to remote learning privacy, online proctoring, surveillance, and vendor data sharing. From late 2022, generative artificial intelligence, ChatGPT, algorithmic bias, ethical artificial intelligence, and artificial intelligence literacy became central. The 2024-2025 frontier connected responsible artificial intelligence with high-risk education systems, human oversight, auditability, and data minimization in large language models. The study argues that compliance is necessary but insufficient. A mature governance model must connect legal duties, institutional processes, technical controls, and educational judgment.

items.title: From Digital Interaction to Emotional Awareness: Artificial Intelligence, Non-Cognitive Skills and Cyberbullying
items.abstract: The widespread diffusion of digital technologies has transformed educational contexts, reshaping how students communicate, learn, and build social relationships. While digital platforms and social networks offer important opportunities for participation and access to knowledge, they have also contributed to new forms of relational vulnerability. Within this scenario, bullying and cyberbullying represent major educational challenges, negatively affecting psychological well-being, academic achievement, and school life. Cyberbullying differs from traditional bullying because it transcends the temporal and spatial boundaries of school, amplifying the impact of aggression through online dissemination. These phenomena are often associated with limited socio-emotional competencies, including empathy, emotional self-regulation, and conflict management. At the same time, artificial intelligence, social robotics, and emotionally aware technologies are redefining the relationship between education, learning, and social interaction. Although these tools may foster empathy and relational awareness, they also raise ethical concerns regarding emotional simulation, privacy, and the authenticity of human relationships. items.title: From Digital Victims to Cyber Offenders Children, Artificial Intelligence and the Emerging Challenges of Criminal Accountability in India
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence intensifies children's dual position in digital environments. A child may be impersonated, groomed, profiled, extorted or depicted in synthetic sexual content; the same child may experiment with generative systems, automated deception or unauthorised-access tools and thereby become a child in conflict with law. This paper asks whether Indian law protects the first child without adultifying the second. Doctrinal analysis shows a substantial but fragmented framework. POCSO and Section 67B of the Information Technology Act address child sexual exploitation material, while the 2024 Supreme Court decision in Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish adopts a purpose-sensitive approach to possession, viewing and reporting. Yet entirely synthetic depictions that do not involve an identifiable or actual child raise unresolved questions of statutory language and harm. The 2026 amendments to the Intermediary Rules now regulate synthetically generated information through user declarations, labelling and due diligence, but do not independently define every deepfake as a crime. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act's child-specific Section 9 and the corresponding final 2025 Rules were enacted but, under the notified phased commencement, were not yet operational on 19 August 2026. For children accused of AI-assisted conduct, the Juvenile Justice Act remains adequate in principle because it demands individualised, rehabilitative inquiry; technical ability is evidence, not a proxy for maturity or mens rea. The paper recommends a child-specific, risk-based AI framework joining safety-by-design, precise synthetic-CSAM coverage, data minimisation, platform duties, evidence standards, diversion and specialised rehabilitation.

items.title: From Energy Input to Orbital Decay: Thermospheric Density and LEO Satellite Response to the May 2024 Gannon Geomagnetic Storm
items.abstract: The May 2024 super geomagnetic storm provided a rare opportunity to investigate the full-chain impact of extreme space weather on the thermosphere and Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. This study presents, for the first time, an end-to-end quantitative analysis that links high-latitude energy input, thermospheric density response, multi-model performance evaluation, and satellite orbital decay. High-latitude Joule heating increased from ~2 mW/m2 during the quiet period to 112 mW/m2 during the main phase. The hemispherically integrated heating peaked at 1822 GW, and the enhanced heating persisted for approximately 18–20 h. Swarm-A observations show that the orbital-mean neutral density at ~470 km increased by a factor of 4.5 relative to quiet-time levels. However, DTM2020, JB2008, NRLMSIS 2.0, and TIEGCM2.0 all underestimated the magnitude of this enhancement, with mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) values of 32.6%, 39.0%, 60.8%, and 40.6%, respectively. Coupling these models to the High Precision Orbit Propagator (HPOP) shows that the China Space Station (CSS) decay rates are 0.5–0.7 km/day during the main phase, about 2–3 times the quiet-time values. These predictions agree with Two-Line Element (TLE) derived semi-major axis decay trends, but significant magnitude discrepancies persist among different models, indicating that thermospheric model selection is a crucial uncertainty source in orbit prediction. A statistical analysis of Space-Track TLE data for LEO population (<1000 km) quantifies decay distribution across altitudes, providing direct references for space situational awareness and orbit maintenance strategies.

items.title: From experience to narrative: artificial intelligence and digital storytelling in the processes of awareness within education
items.abstract: This paper offers a reflection centred on the synergy between Mindfulness-based Self-Awareness Workshops, Digital Storytelling and Generative Artificial Intelligence in contemporary educational contexts. The aim is to investigate the implications for students' individual and collective identity exploration processes and for the development of critical, reflective and emotionally oriented digital literacy. In this context, digital media and AI are not regarded as mere technical tools, nor as a shortcut to delegating thought to machines, but as a symbolic extension of the mind and body (Di Domenico et al., 2025), serving to enhance self-awareness and relational responsibility. The training programme is structured according to the perspective of Embodied Cognitive Science (ECS), recognising that cognition is deeply rooted in the body and influenced by emotional experience. items.title: From Functional Nanomaterials to Trustworthy Wearable Sensing Systems: A Cross-Layer Review of Bioelectronic Interfaces, Wireless and Power Integration, Artificial Intelligence Inference/Interpretation, and Human-Centred Validation
items.abstract: Material-level sensitivity or conductivity alone does not determine whether a wearable sensor produces trustworthy data. The signal must survive body coupling, packaging, wireless transfer, power constraints, and algorithmic interpretation. This cross-layer critical review examines six connected evidence streams: functional nanomaterial platforms, epidermal and implantable bioelectronic interfaces, wireless readout and power, integrated wearable platforms, artificial intelligence (AI)-based interpretation, and human-centred applications. Hysteresis and drift, interface instability, motion and environmental exposure, readout and power limits, placement and calibration dependence, and inter-user variability can degrade information across these layers. Robustness testing and claim-matched validation are needed to establish what the resulting outputs support. We therefore compare technologies through the failure modes and evidence requirements that persist after integration, rather than through isolated peak metrics. The synthesis offers conditional material-selection criteria for specific device roles, distinguishes demonstrated component functions from application-level claims, and identifies the reporting conditions and use-dependent validation priorities needed to interpret those claims.

items.title: From generative AI literacy to perceived employability: technological self-efficacy, career adaptability and internship quality in Taiwan's TVET
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines how perceived generative AI literacy (GAIL) becomes employability-relevant for technical and vocational education and training (TVET) students through technological self-efficacy and career adaptability, and whether internship quality strengthens this pathway. Design/methodology/approach 526 Taiwanese TVET students with internship experience was analysed using standardised composite-score path analysis, 5,000-resample nonparametric bootstrapping, moderation tests and subgroup diagnostics. Findings All six hypotheses were supported. Perceived GAIL was positively associated with technological self-efficacy, career adaptability and perceived employability through the hypothesised serial pathway. Internship quality strengthened the first-stage association. Supplementary records linked perceived GAIL with task performance and supervisor ratings, and perceived employability with later employment and job fit. Research limitations/implications Although supplementary performance, rater, supervisor and follow-up records reduce sole dependence on self-report, the primary structural model remains observational and perception-based. Future research should pre-register performance assessments and test measurement invariance across TVET tracks. Practical implications TVET providers should teach GenAI literacy as responsible task performance, not mere tool use, and connect it to supervised internship tasks, feedback and transparent skill signalling. Originality/value The study specifies a GenAI-focused, theory-grounded employability pathway and identifies internship quality as a workplace-learning condition under which perceived digital competence is more strongly associated with career confidence.

items.title: From Human–Computer Interaction to Human–AI Collaboration: A New Paradigm for Intelligent Management Information Systems
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the way individuals interact with digital technologies and Information Systems (IS), requiring a rethinking of some traditional assumptions underlying Human–Computer Interaction (HCI). In Management Information Systems (MIS), this transformation extends beyond the design of usable interfaces toward the development of intelligent systems that can actively support, augment, and collaborate with human users. This chapter examines the evolution from HCI to Human–AI Collaboration (HAC) and discusses its implications for the development of intelligent MIS. It first establishes the conceptual foundations of HCI, including human factors, user-centered design, usability, accessibility, and user experience (UX). It then examines the emergence of Human–AI Interaction (HAI) and the transition from computers as passive tools toward intelligent interaction partners. Building on this foundation, the chapter conceptualizes HAC through complementary human and AI capabilities, human oversight, AI-augmented decision-making, and increasingly autonomous AI systems. Particular attention is given to human-centered design, Generative AI, conversational and multimodal interfaces, intelligent UX, and the different roles humans may assume in AI-enabled environments, including interaction, evaluation, supervision, and, under appropriate conditions, collaboration with AI systems. The chapter further discusses ethical and organizational challenges, including algorithmic bias, privacy, transparency, accountability, automation bias, and human agency. It argues that the future of MIS will increasingly depend not only on technological intelligence but also on how effectively HAC is designed, governed, and integrated into organizational work.
